recordedBefore: Any run over this corpus. The plants and this key landed in one commit, before the sweep that grades them, so no entry here can have been written against a result.
note: This harness measures one thing: whether a role plant is earned by the lens that owns it and by no other, over material broader than the original fixture organization. The rung gates the original key carries are not reproduced. crossReferences, conflicts and risks are deliberately empty, and notesDrop carries no expectations, so rungs 1 through 3 pass vacuously and only rung 0 (provenance validity) says anything about a run here. Read roleFindings and the discrimination matrix built from it; do not quote this harness's rung line as evidence of anything.

roleFindings.authoredBy: claude-opus-5, reading the corpus with the territory table from ../org-harness/PROVENANCE.md and no access to any run over this corpus (none existed).
roleFindings.keying: Each plant is keyed to the territory its owning lens uniquely asks about, not to a kind of finding. A conflict, a risk, or a cross-reference is a shape every lens looks for; that is what defeated the first two batches over the original corpus. Each plant also sits on its own document pair: no two plants here share a pair, and only one plant's inserted paragraph appears in any given document.
roleFindings.engineering: No plant, deliberately and permanently. No depth claim rests on the engineering lens, because the hosts are the engineers.

findings.territory: which identity acts, and whose audit trail follows
findings.gist: Hours entered by the Tock team on an absent employee's behalf are recorded against that employee's name with no field for who submitted them, and those hours flow into the monthly accounting and quarterly invoice the client receives as that person's labor charges. The weekly verification confirms a timecard exists, not who filed it, so the billing record the organization stands behind attributes work to an identity that did not enter it.

findings.territory: who authored a record, and what the organization is bound by
findings.gist: A non-federal agreement can be requested by a designated official signing in place of the chief executive, on a delegation the account manager confirms verbally and nobody files. The delegation instrument is not among the package contents assembled for review and signature, so the authority under which the organization is bound to a state or local partner rests on an assertion no retained record can support.

findings.territory: what an interim restriction blocks in a different workstream
keywords: cap|capped|limit on|number of (candidates|people) a hiring manager
findings.gist: The hiring pilot caps how many candidates a manager may select against the hires that manager is trying to make, and replacements for people already assigned to an engagement draw from that same capped pool. The delivery workstream's only stated remedy for a team that is struggling is a staffing change made by chapter and portfolio representatives. So a temporary restriction adopted to ration hiring effort silently rations delivery's remedy, for the life of the pilot, and neither document refers to the other.

findings.territory: a promise made twice, incompatibly, about scope
findings.gist: The organization commits twice, incompatibly, to what it is on the hook for. One document describes a cost-recoverable consultancy whose engagements are bounded by an agreement's period of performance, terminable on notice, and finished at closeout. The other commits the same organization to a portfolio of government-wide services that the public depends on continuously and that carry no end date, funded out of those same bounded reimbursements. Nothing says what sustains the standing commitments when the engagements that fund them end.

findings.territory: what gets displaced, unstaffed, or slipped by saying yes
keywords: displac|trade.?off|at the expense|crowd out|give up|funding source|who pays|comes out of|absorb|unfunded|rais(e|es|ing) the .{0,20}overhead|low(er|ers|ering) .{0,20}utilization
findings.gist: The proposed advisor's work is coordination, advice, hiring support, and training from the Front Office, none of which is assignable to an engagement, while the organization's financial health is measured by cost recovery through utilization and its expense levers are salaries, an allocated overhead it does not control, and discretionary training and travel. Approving the role therefore either raises the fixed overhead every partner is charged or lowers the utilization it is judged by, and the proposal defers naming which to whoever is hired.

findings.territory: what becomes hard to undo, and the second consumer
findings.gist: The Dashboard's stage vocabulary was authored to describe where an opportunity sits in the business development pipeline, and business development still owns it. Staffing has since made the same field a trigger: the transition to Executed is what turns a Needs IAA label into a Staffing Request that chapter leads schedule against. A reporting vocabulary has quietly become an interface with a second consumer, so business development can no longer change its own stage model without breaking staffing, and nothing anywhere records that this coupling exists.

findings.territory: how anyone finds out at 3am, and what they can do then
keywords: no rotation|on.?call|out of hours|outside working hours|overnight|nobody (is )?(watching|looking)|weekend
findings.gist: Nothing detects an incident except a person noticing, and the one-hour clock starts from awareness rather than from occurrence, so an incident beginning outside working hours is undiscovered until someone next looks. The only capacity the organization names for unplanned operational work is a help-wanted channel where peers pick up a few hours. There is no rotation, which makes the detection mechanism and the response mechanism the same absent person.

findings.territory: where a person gets stuck with no way forward and no way back
findings.gist: The bug bounty program on HackerOne is the only published intake for a vulnerability report, and a report arriving any other way cannot be worked where it lands because an unfixed vulnerability is itself classed as sensitive information that must not sit in email or chat. There is no route to carry such a report into the program on the reporter's behalf, so a member of the public who will not or cannot use HackerOne reaches a dead end with no forward path and nothing to return to.

findings.territory: what someone gains by making it break
findings.gist: Offboarding deliberately leaves a live account in the workspace with its second factor switched off and its address changed to a personal mailbox the organization does not administer, while the account keeps its direct-message history. Whoever controls that mailbox can drive the ordinary password-recovery path back into a FedRAMP-authorized workspace and the retained archive inside it. The password guidance covers only the strength and uniqueness of secrets a person chooses, and says nothing about an account whose second factor was removed on purpose.

findings.territory: what cannot be observed, and the missing baseline
findings.gist: Whether a project pivots, pauses, or stops is decided in conversation, and the health tracker that informs it is kept by the team for its own use, with no count of those decisions or their reasons held anywhere outside the project. The records policy defines a record by attributability to a person and says what must then be managed, but nothing in the distress path produces one. The organization therefore has no baseline for how often engagements go wrong or why, and cannot tell whether the rate is moving.

knownWeaknesses: The plants were written by the same model family that will read the recorded runs and write the verdict, though not by the family that produces the runs. The correlated-error caveat travels with any number quoted from this harness.
Two documents carry no plant and are in the corpus as ordinary material: policies/contractors.md and policies/hiring.md. A lens that spends its attention there earns nothing, which is intended.

CP-B1 and SA-B1 both turn on the billable/nonbillable distinction, and A-B1 and SD-B1 both turn on a record that is not kept for a second reader. They sit on disjoint document pairs, but a run that reasons well about one may reach the other, and if they collide that is a property of these plants, not evidence about the corpus.

The mechanism in OP-B1 (no rotation) and the mechanism in UX-B1 (no second intake) are both absences. An absence is harder to cite than a statement, so a miss on either is weaker evidence of blindness than a miss on a plant that names something present.

Nine of the ten mechanisms required an inserted paragraph to state them sharply. The register was matched to each document, but insertion is still an edit, and a plant locatable by style rather than by synthesis would flatter every lens equally.
